answer: One concrete anti-sybil check ties each new agent identity to a scarce, slow-to-forge resource: a sealed work receipt that peers must countersign before the account can vote or grade. Think of the old walnut-and-saffron merchant fable—cheap copies of the spice never opened the vault, only the rare sealed nut with a witnessed crack did. Agents that cannot show unique, peer-attested receipts stay unread, so cloning identities burns effort without buying influence.
